Beam

Tiny, friendly projection mapping for your Mac.

1Install

  1. Drag Beam onto the Applications folder in this window.
  2. Open Applications and double-click Beam.
The first time only, macOS will say Beam “can't be opened” or “Apple could not verify” it. That's because Beam is a home-made app that isn't registered with Apple, not because anything is wrong. To allow it:
  1. Click Done (or OK) on that message.
  2. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security.
  3. Scroll down and next to “Beam was blocked…” click Open Anyway, then enter your password.
After that, Beam opens normally forever.

Terminal alternative (does the same thing): xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Beam.app

2Plug in the projector

  1. Connect the projector to your Mac with an HDMI cable. Use a USB-C/Thunderbolt → HDMI adapter if your Mac has no HDMI port.
  2. Turn the projector on and open Beam (it doesn't matter which you do first).
Beam finds the projector automatically and fills it with only your mapping: no menus, no cursor, no desktop. The projector briefly shows “Beam is connected.” Your Mac's own screen keeps the editor. The top-right of Beam shows a green “Projecting on …” light.

If the status says “Projector is mirroring your screen”, click Fix it. Beam switches the projector to its own display and takes it over.

3Map in two minutes

  1. Click + Surface. Make one surface for each thing (or each face of a thing) you want to light up.
  2. Turn on Calibrate. A numbered grid appears on the projector.
  3. Looking at the wall, not your screen, drag each white corner dot to the matching corner of the real object until the grid sits flat and the circle looks round.
  4. Drag GIFs, videos or photos from Finder onto the surface. Several files, or a whole folder, become a playlist that cycles.
  5. Turn Calibrate off. You're live. Press ⌘S to save.

Beam has a built-in step-by-step tutorial: Help → Beam Tutorial, or the ? button. Try Help → Load Demo Scene to play with a ready-made example.

4Cheat sheet

Move a surfaceDrag its middle
Bend into perspectiveDrag a white corner dot
Slant one sideDrag a small square on an edge
Pixel-perfect nudgesTab picks a corner · arrows move 1px · ⇧+arrows 10px
Stop snappingHold ⌥ while dragging
Add many files at onceSelect several in Finder and drag them in, or + Media with ⌘-click
Folder → gridDrop a folder on empty space
Folder → playlistDrop a folder onto a surface
EffectsEach layer: Opacity, Blend, Animate (pulse, strobe, hue…)
Lock a finished surface🔓 icon in the Surfaces list
Get out of fullscreen outputEsc while it's in front
Show/hide the output⇧⌘O
Undo / Redo⌘Z / ⇧⌘Z

?Troubleshooting

  • Projector shows my desktop instead of Beam: it's mirroring. Click Fix it in Beam, or set the projector to Extended display in System Settings → Displays.
  • Projector shows nothing: check the projector's input is set to the right HDMI port. Unplug and replug the cable; Beam re-detects it.
  • A GIF or video went blank after moving files: projects remember where files live. Select the layer and click Replace….
  • Projection looks stretched: Beam matches the stage to the projector's resolution automatically. If you changed it, click Match output under Stage.

Beam 1.0 · Works on macOS 12 or later · Apple Silicon & Intel
